contract.note: The contract scores the claim on a plain reading even though it notes the statement is explicitly tentative. Under policy, a plain reading applies only to firm language, and hedged claims are not scored. The evaluator also supplied its own meaning for 'real issue'.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the absolute '100% of time' threshold and all three failure types. 'Unruly beasts' is rhetorical framing; the testable part is the claim about the research state.

contract.note: Reading 'nobody knows' as the publicly established research state in 2022, up to the post date, is ordinary and fair. Separating lower failure rates from guaranteed zero failures matches his absolute wording.

evidence.note: OpenAI, January 2022: InstructGPT still produces toxic output and made-up facts, and reliable refusal is called an open problem. It is a company disclosure, but it admits limits against the company's interest.
DeepMind's Sparrow preprint, September 2022: evidence supports only 78% of factual answers, and the model breaks its rules 8% of the time under probing. No complete protection.
Galactica model card, 15 November 2022: explicitly gives no guarantee of truthful output and says hallucination persists.

reviews.rationale: Three 2022 sources from leading labs describe their best safety methods as still producing toxic, rule-breaking, or made-up output, and treat reliable prevention as unsolved. The packet shows no method that guaranteed all three protections. That matches the support condition for the state of research when the post appeared.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. The staffing clause he marked 'apparently' is correctly left out.

semantics.note: Faithful to the wording. Grammatically Amazon is the subject of (b), but the clause plainly means Alexa. 'Seems clumsy' is an impressionistic comparison; the feature-history clause is a firm factual assertion.

contract.note: Marcus gave no threshold for 'significant' and no start date. The evaluator chose roughly 2019 onward and counts new capabilities actually released to users. That is an ordinary reading of his broad wording, but the result depends on it, and it rests on the evaluator's judgement that the 2021 launches were significant.

evidence.note: Amazon's dated record of the November 2021 Conversation Mode launch: wake-word-free use by several people at once on Echo Show devices. A company disclosure, but adequate to show the feature was available. It is not GPT-3-like conversation.
Amazon's March 2021 general-availability post for Alexa Conversations, listing user-facing additions such as book recommendations and Ring doorbell greetings within the period.
Amazon, June 2022: Alexa needs to generalise beyond special-purpose modules. Consistent with Marcus's point about limits, but it gives no comparison with GPT-3.

reviews.rationale: Dated 2021 Amazon release records show new interaction capabilities reaching users: Conversation Mode, plus experiences built with Alexa Conversations. That defeats 'hasn't added significant features in years' on the contract's reading. The GPT-3 comparison is unsettled because no head-to-head evaluation was found. The result depends on treating these launches as significant.
